The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed the house to him, he owned both the dominant and servient parcels, so the easement was extinguished by merger. His later warranty deed to the purchaser didn't revive it. The purchaser also has no implied easement, because the man never used the path while he owned both parcels, and the house has other access to the highway, so there is no easement by necessity.

CONFIDENCE: 85
